title: Throw a checked failure out of a stream lambda

blocks.text: `Function`, `Consumer` and the other standard functional interfaces declare no checked exceptions, so a lambda body that throws an `IOException` does not compile. Write `TextLengths.lengths(List<String> names, TextSource source)` with a stream: map each name to the length of `source.fetch(name)`, in order.
When `fetch` throws an `IOException`, catch it inside the lambda and throw an `UncheckedIOException` with the message `Could not read <name>`.
The unchecked wrapper is only a vehicle out of the lambda: whoever catches it must still be able to get at the original `IOException`.

cases.says: The length of every fetched text is returned, in the order of the names.
A failed fetch leaves the lambda as an UncheckedIOException whose cause is the source's IOException.
The wrapper's message names the text that failed: "Could not read b.txt".

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A lambda for a standard functional interface cannot throw a checked exception, so it wraps it in an unchecked one.
